title: Account Saver Catalyst Playbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a rapid-response playbook designed for mid-to-high ARR accounts showing early-to-moderate renewal risk. Goal is to standardize assessment, escalate efficiently to execs, and run prioritized save plays that are measurable within a 30-90 day runway.

Scope:
- Applies to accounts where the internal Renewal Risk Score is >= 0.6 (see scoring below)
- Intended for CSM-led interventions with AE and Solutions Engineering support
- Not a full churn forensic — this is a prescriptive, time-boxed remediation guide

Quick glossary:
- CSM: Customer Success Manager
- AE: Account Executive
- SE: Solutions Engineer / Technical Success
- RO: Renewal Ops (contracts/pricing support)
- Exec Escalation: notified executive(s) from customer and Redwood when threshold reached

1) Triage & Risk Assessment (first 72 hours)
- Gather one-pager: latest usage trends (7/30/90d), top 5 support tickets, NPS/CSAT points, outstanding P0s, contract renewal date, revenue at risk.
- Run Renewal Risk Score (weighted):
  - Usage decline (30d drop % / 2) weight 0.35
  - Active P0/P1 tickets (0/1/2+) weight 0.25
  - Exec engagement (none=1, sporadic=0.5, active=0) weight 0.15
  - QBR/ROI milestone missed (yes=1/no=0) weight 0.15
  - Payment/contract issues (billing dispute/notice) weight 0.10
- Score interpretation: 0-0.3 low risk, 0.31-0.59 moderate, 0.6-1.0 high risk

Immediate actions checklist (CSM):
- Create "Account Saver" folder in drive and log initial findings (attach charts/tickets).
- Contact AE and SE: 1-hour standup to align on root causes and short plays.
- Update customer record with initial triage and set 7-day action plan.

2) Playbook Ladder (prioritized, time-boxed plays)
- Day 0–7: Rapid Confidence Restores (Tactical)
  - Proof-of-value demo: 30–45m targeted demo addressing primary friction (CSM+SE).
  - Quick-win config + enablement: deploy template fix or runbook; measure immediate usage bump.
  - SLA remediation: if P0/P1 caused churn risk, offer prioritized response window + weekly status.
  - Compensation leash: limited short-term credits (RO + AE sign-off) — document and timebox.

- Day 7–21: Operational Repair (Short-term)
  - Usage campaign: targeted outreach to power-users with guided tasks to re-engage.
  - Integrations/Onboarding unblock: SE-led migration sprints or scope reduction.
  - Product workaround + roadmap commitment: log feature request; provide ETA or alternate path.

- Day 21–60: Strategic Re-anchor (Medium-term)
  - ROI revalidation: deliver updated ROI spreadsheet with real customer metrics.
  - Executive alignment: AE + CSM request 30-minute exec working session to restart sponsorship.
  - Contract reframing: RO explores term/structure changes (milestone-based payments, opt-down seats).

- Day 60–90+: Salvage or Transition (Long-term)
  - If progress: convert to growth plan with milestones and KPIs in QBR cadence.
  - If no progress: prepare offboarding playbook and knowledge transfer to minimize disruption.

3) Exec Escalation Framework
- Trigger: any of the following -> Renewal Risk Score >= 0.75, missed contractual SLA causing material impact, or customer exec asks for direct exec contact.
- Escalation ladder:
  - Level 1 (Urgent): CSM -> AE -> Head of CS (note, escalate via Slack huddle + 1-pager)
  - Level 2 (Critical): Head of CS -> VP Customer Success -> Sales Leader -> Chief Customer Officer (formal sync + exec brief)
  - External cadence: aim for 48–72 hour turnaround for executive outreach and a next-step commitment.

One-page Exec Brief template (for Redwood execs to send to customer execs):
- Subject: "30-min: [Customer] — Focused plan to restore ROI before renewal"
- 3-line synopsis: highlight top-impact issue, immediate remediation, and how Redwood will de-risk their renewal.
- Key metrics: revenue at risk, delta in usage, number of active P1/P0 items, committed timeline.
- Ask: 15–30 minutes from customer execs to validate plan + one decision (approve pilot, adjust contract, grant additional time).

4) Mitigation Matrix (who does what)
- CSM: owns health story, daily standups first week, customer comms templates, usage campaigns.
- AE: commercial options, pricing/credit approvals, exec outreach.
- SE: technical remediation, fast patches, runbooks, migration scope.
- RO: contract edits, pilot pricing, approvals for concessions.
- Legal: only escalate if contract terms require nonstandard amendment.

5) Communication templates (copy-paste friendly)
- Slack ping to AE: "Heads-up: [Account] flagged high-risk (score=0.78). 1-hr triage call now? Findings: usage -45% 30d, 2 P1s open. Proposed immediate play: PV demo + 2-week SE sprint. 
  Link: <drive>/account-saver/[account]"
- Customer email subject: "Proposed 30-day plan to restore outcomes for [Customer Name]"
- Customer email body (short): "Thanks for the candid feedback. We’ve scoped a focused 30-day plan to address X,Y,Z. Can we align on a 30-min sync this week to walk through it? Attendees: your sponsor + CSM + SE. Attached: one-page plan + ROI snapshot."

6) Measurement & Escalation Signals
- Weekly checkpoint metrics: active seats, daily users, P1/P0 count, feature adoption for target flows, NPS/CSAT for support touchpoints.
- Green = measureable improvement (>=15% usage uplift OR closure of P1s); Amber = partial progress; Red = no movement.
- If Red at Week 2 -> escalate to Level 1. If Red at Week 4 -> escalate to Level 2 and consider contractual options.

7) QBR / Renewal Tracker snapshot (fields to include)
- Account name, ARR, renewal date, Renewal Risk Score, top-3 issues, last 90d usage trend, last touchpoint, next milestone, current play, executive sponsor (Redwood), suggested concession (if any), notes
- Recommended cadence: CSM updates tracker weekly; AE validates concession fields before any customer-facing offer.

8) Example save plays (concrete examples)
- Fast POC: 30-day pilot at reduced rate, with clear acceptance criteria tied to measurable usage.
- Outcome-based credits: 50% credit applied if agreed ROI metric not met after 60 days.
- Dedicated SE blitz: 2-week onsite/remote sprint to complete migration lift.
- Service bundle rethink: temporarily move to consumption-based billing for high-variance workloads.

9) Handoffs & Closing the Loop
- If successful: create follow-up QBR agenda that converts save to growth, assign milestones and signal to renew ops to lock new terms.
- If unsuccessful: complete offboarding checklist, final knowledge transfer, and collect learnings in the "saver-retros" doc.

Appendix A — Quick scoring example:
- 30d usage drop 40% -> 0.4 * 0.35 = 0.14
- 2 P1s open -> normalized 0.8 * 0.25 = 0.20
- Exec engagement sporadic -> 0.5 * 0.15 = 0.075
- Missed ROI milestone -> 1 * 0.15 = 0.15
- No payment issues -> 0 * 0.10 = 0.00
- Total = 0.565 -> Moderate risk (but trending high).

Appendix B — Notes to CSM (practical tips)
- Keep comms short and outcome-focused; use a 1-pg visual for execs.
- Document every concession in the drive folder and tag AE/RO for approvals.
- Prefer measurable, time-boxed offers over open-ended discounts.
- Use Slack huddles for rapid alignment, but always follow up with a one-pager in Drive for auditability.

Draft status and next steps:
- This is a working draft. Please add real case snippets (anonymized) under the "examples" subfolder.
- Action: request feedback from Head of CS and two senior AEs by 2026-03-10.

-- end of doc --
